Saved jamovi examples

Source: GUI_EXAMPLES.md

All nine module analyses have a synthetic example in data/. Analyses were added, configured and saved through the jamovi GUI on macOS, jamovi 28.17.0.0. The fixture generator creates data only; it does not construct analysis options or results. Open an .omv directly with jamovi. After rebuilding and installing this source, the examples also appear under Open → Data Library → jsurvival, using the titles in jamovi/0000.yaml.

The cohort examples contain 150 independent simulated patients, 106 observed events and 44 right-censored observations. time and followup are months. event uses 1 for the event and 0 for censoring. Control and Treatment are illustrative group labels; the data do not establish a treatment effect.

File in data/ Saved analysis and selected arguments
singlearm_example.omv Single Arm Survival: Kaplan-Meier, confidence intervals, risk table, censor marks, person-time rates and summaries.
survival_example.omv Survival Analysis: group comparison, age adjustment using age, adjusted curves, PH diagnostics, KM with confidence intervals/risk table/censor marks, and RMST. rmst_tau = 0 selects the automatic horizon.
survivalcont_example.omv Continuous-marker survival: marker, exploratory optimal cut-off, KM groups and exported cut-off group. A selected cut-off requires independent validation.
multisurvival_example.omv Multivariable Cox: categorical group and stage, continuous age and marker, finalfit forest and PH diagnostics. No interaction is fitted.
lassocox_example.omv LASSO Cox: the same four predictors, explicit event/censor levels, five CV folds, lambda.min, seed 123456 and internal standardization; CV, coefficient and apparent risk-group plots.
oddsratio_example.omv Firth logistic regression of event on group, age and marker, with explanations and the nomogram safeguard requested. See the expected warnings below.
datetimeconverter_example.omv Eight rows; iso_date, YMD, UTC, preview 10, year/month/day extraction and exported year. Also contains mixed_date with malformed text and numeric excel_date for further exploration.
outcomeorganizer_example.omv Overall survival: explicit AWOD/AWD/DOD/DOOC mapping, follow-up and invented patient IDs, diagnostics, visualization and exported recoded outcome. Both death categories are events.
timeinterval_example.omv ISO start/end dates, standardized months (days / 30.4375), quality metrics, summary and exported calculated time.

Options exercised in the GUI

  • DateTime: automatic versus explicit YMD, system timezone versus UTC, component extraction and output. A preview of 5 correctly produced the documented 10–100 constraint error; setting 10 recovered the analysis before saving.
  • Time intervals: days versus months, calendar versus standardized duration, quality metrics and exported time. The saved example explicitly uses standardized months. Date rounding means these intervals need not exactly equal the original continuous simulated survival times.
  • Outcomes: overall survival and competing risks. The latter retained 82 disease deaths, 24 other-cause deaths and 44 censored observations; the saved OS example has 106 events. No unknown status was coded as alive.
  • Survival: plots, confidence/risk/censor displays, person-time, age adjustment, adjusted curves, PH diagnostics, RMST and exploratory cut-off output across the relevant examples. The saved RMST horizon is automatic, not a fixed 24 months.
  • Multivariable: categorical and continuous predictors, forest and PH plots. The reopened interaction panel listed all four available predictors. An interaction model and the alternate forest style were not completed in this GUI pass.
  • LASSO: 10, 6 and 5 folds, and the 1-SE and minimum-error rules. The final saved settings are five folds and minimum error. Figures were explicitly rendered, saved again and visually verified after reopening.
  • Odds ratios: ordinary and Firth logistic fits and explanatory output. Requesting the nomogram with Firth correctly displays that it is unavailable rather than drawing a nomogram from a different fitted model.

The odds-ratio file deliberately keeps the Firth nomogram warning. Diagnostic metrics also wait for an explicitly selected diagnostic predictor and its positive and negative levels. The logistic model and forest are complete. Its binary outcome records whether an event was observed during varying follow-up; these odds ratios are not fixed-horizon survival risks, diagnostic accuracy estimates or risk ratios.

Verification and remaining limitation

Rscript --vanilla data-raw/validate-gui-examples.R passes 90 checks: nine matching analysis identities, completed status and no result-element errors; exact catalog metadata; row/event counts; cached plot resources; exported year and interval arithmetic; overall-survival mapping; an independent survival::coxph comparison of the displayed multivariable HRs; LASSO coefficient/HR arithmetic and saved tuning; and the Firth safeguard. All nine ZIP integrity checks passed; file hashes are recorded in data-raw/gui-examples-sha256.txt. Compiler --prepare also passed in an isolated copy, copied the examples and preserved all ten dataset entries (including the existing histopathology example). The compiler was given the observed app version explicitly because its automatic app-version probe failed. Completed status alone did not establish that plots had been cached: the initial LASSO save lacked images. Recalculation, figure rendering and a further GUI save resolved that file; the final archive contains all three requested plot images.

DateTime’s missing component row still displays NaN in some native numeric preview cells. Inspection finds literal "NA" strings in the serialized year/month component columns, while the day column uses a proper missing cell. Parsing counts are correct (8 total, 1 originally missing, 7 parsed, 0 failed; percentages 100%, 12.5%, 87.5%, 0%), and the exported year contains a genuine missing value. This preview presentation issue remains open and is distinct from the repaired parsing-count denominator issue.

These bounded GUI and arithmetic checks do not complete every option combination, theme, export format, interaction model or final release acceptance check. The installed candidate used for creation has SHA-256 81774a0042a441426473dc903964418fdb72993f95557343b7296a752bb95646; the source candidate was subsequently rebuilt for catalog wording as recorded in RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md. Neither existing archive includes these newly added data files: rebuild before library submission. No module was submitted or published.

Maintaining the files

  • data-raw/gui-examples.R reproduces the initial synthetic data only, with seed
    1. It refuses to overwrite saved examples. Recreate data in a clean copy if needed, then add/configure analyses through the GUI again.
  • data-raw/gui-examples.yaml is the maintained metadata for the new examples. Rscript --vanilla data-raw/register-gui-examples.R uses the umbrella’s document_module_omv() helper to append missing entries and verify them. prepare() preserves the datasets section; no unsupported configuration key is needed. Analysis registry entries remain generated.
  • The validator reads the integer nominal output in the outcome example directly from the archive because jmvReadWrite::read_omv() currently rejects that Integer/Output combination. This is a reader limitation, not a jamovi file error; the archive is not modified by validation.
